name: Figure Matrices
blurb: Four boxes. One is empty. What goes there?
childIntro: Look at the top two boxes. Something changed. Now make the same change happen in the bottom row.
howItWorks: A two-by-two grid of shapes with the bottom-right box missing. The top row shows a change. The left column shows a different change. The answer has to obey both at once. CogAT keeps this two-by-two shape all the way from kindergarten to grade 5, so the format never surprises a child. What grows is the number of things changing at the same time.
parentTip: The single most common mistake is spotting one change and stopping. Ask your child to say out loud what changed going across, then what changed going down, before looking at the answers. Also ask what stayed the same. What does not change is as much of a clue as what does.

questions.prompt: The top row changes. Make the same change in the bottom row.

figure.alt: Top row: a white circle, then a blue circle. Bottom row: a white square, then an empty box.

questions.explanation: Going across the top, the circle gets filled in with colour. The shape stays a circle. So the square must get filled in too, and stay a square. That is the filled blue square.
questions.strategy: Say it out loud: 'across, it fills in.' Then do the same thing to the shape below.

questions.prompt: Finish the bottom row the same way.

figure.alt: Top row: a small yellow star, then a big yellow star. Bottom row: a small yellow heart, then an empty box.

questions.explanation: Across the top, the star gets bigger. Nothing else changes. So the heart gets bigger too. It stays a heart and it stays yellow.
questions.strategy: When only the size changes, check that the colour and the shape stay exactly the same.

questions.prompt: Finish the bottom row the same way.

figure.alt: Top row: an empty pink slanted rectangle, then a big empty pink slanted rectangle. Bottom row: an empty pink arrow, then an empty box.

questions.explanation: Going across, the shape gets bigger. Choice b did not get bigger.
questions.strategy: Say the change out loud, then do exactly that to the shape below.

questions.prompt: Finish the bottom row the same way.

figure.alt: Top row: a small purple flag, then a small empty purple flag. Bottom row: a small purple house, then an empty box.

questions.explanation: Going across, the shape empties out. Choice b stayed filled in.
questions.strategy: Say the change out loud, then do exactly that to the shape below.

questions.prompt: Finish the bottom row the same way.

figure.alt: Top row: an empty yellow right triangle, then a small empty yellow right triangle. Bottom row: an empty yellow square, then an empty box.

questions.explanation: Going across, the shape gets smaller. Choice b did not get smaller.
questions.strategy: Say the change out loud, then do exactly that to the shape below.

questions.prompt: How many go in the empty box?

figure.alt: Top row: one green circle, then three green circles. Bottom row: one green triangle, then an empty box.

questions.explanation: Across the top, one circle becomes three circles. So one triangle becomes three triangles. Count them: you need three, not two.
questions.strategy: Count the top row first. Say the numbers out loud: one, then three.

questions.prompt: Something changes across the top. Do the same on the bottom.

figure.alt: Top row: an orange square, then an orange square with stripes. Bottom row: an orange hexagon, then an empty box.

questions.explanation: Across the top, the solid square gets stripes. So the solid hexagon gets stripes too. Choice d has dots, not stripes. That is not the same change.
questions.strategy: Look closely at the pattern inside. Stripes and dots are not the same thing.

questions.prompt: Finish the bottom row the same way.

figure.alt: Top row: a small empty green right triangle, then a small empty green right triangle, turned a quarter turn. Bottom row: a small empty green lightning bolt, then an empty box.

questions.explanation: Going across, the shape turns a quarter turn. Choice b did not turn.
questions.strategy: Check what changed AND what stayed the same. Both are clues.

questions.prompt: Finish the bottom row the same way.

figure.alt: Top row: a small pink lightning bolt, then a small pink lightning bolt. Bottom row: a small pink pentagon, then an empty box.

questions.explanation: Going across, the shape gets smaller. Choice b did not get smaller.
questions.strategy: Check what changed AND what stayed the same. Both are clues.

questions.prompt: Finish the bottom row the same way.

figure.alt: Top row: a small yellow star, then a small yellow star. Bottom row: a small yellow kite, then an empty box.

questions.explanation: Going across, the shape gets smaller. Choice b did not get smaller.

questions.prompt: Two things change across the top. Do both on the bottom.

figure.alt: Top row: a small white circle, then a big blue circle. Bottom row: a small white star, then an empty box.

questions.explanation: Two things happen across the top. The circle gets bigger, and it turns blue. The star must do both: get bigger and turn blue. Choice b is blue but still small. Choice c is big but still white.
questions.strategy: When two things change, check both before you pick. Ask: is it the right size AND the right colour?

questions.prompt: Finish the bottom row the same way.

figure.alt: Top row: an empty red moon, then a small empty red moon, turned a quarter turn. Bottom row: an empty red tall rectangle, then an empty box.

questions.explanation: Two things change: the shape gets smaller, and the shape turns a quarter turn. Choice b did not get smaller. Choice c did not turn.
questions.strategy: Two changes means two checks. Go through them one at a time.

questions.prompt: Finish the bottom row the same way.

figure.alt: Top row: a small empty orange six-pointed star, then a small orange six-pointed star, turned a quarter turn. Bottom row: a small empty orange half circle, then an empty box.

questions.explanation: Two things change: the shape turns a quarter turn, and the shape fills in. Choice b did not turn. Choice c never filled in.
questions.strategy: Two changes means two checks. Go through them one at a time.

questions.prompt: Finish the bottom row the same way.

figure.alt: Top row: a teal tall rectangle, then an orange tall rectangle, turned a quarter turn. Bottom row: a teal star, then an empty box.

questions.explanation: Two things change: the color turns orange, and the shape turns a quarter turn. Choice b kept the old color. Choice c did not turn.
questions.strategy: Each wrong answer follows all the rules but one. Find the one that breaks none.

questions.prompt: Finish the bottom row the same way.

figure.alt: Top row: a small empty yellow heart, then a big yellow heart. Bottom row: a small empty yellow plus sign, then an empty box.

questions.strategy: List every change on your fingers, then test the answer against every finger.

questions.strategy: List every change on your fingers, then test the answer against every finger.

figure.alt: Top row: a purple triangle pointing up, then the same triangle pointing down. Bottom row: a purple house shape, then an empty box.

questions.explanation: Across the top the triangle flips all the way upside down. So the house flips all the way upside down too. Choice c only turned it a quarter of the way.
questions.strategy: Turn your head, or turn the iPad, to check how far a shape has spun.

questions.prompt: Finish the bottom row the same way.

figure.alt: Top row: an empty red oval, then a red oval, with upright stripes inside. Bottom row: an empty red house, then an empty box.

questions.explanation: Going across, the inside becomes upright stripes. Choice b did not become upright stripes.

figure.alt: Top row: a green octagon, then four green octagons. Bottom row: a green pentagon, then an empty box.

questions.strategy: Pick one corner of the shape and follow just that corner. It is easier than watching the whole shape.

figure.alt: Top row: three blue squares, then one blue square. Bottom row: three yellow stars, then an empty box.

questions.explanation: Across the top, three squares become one square. So three stars become one star. The number goes down, not up.
questions.strategy: Patterns can shrink as well as grow. Check which direction the number is going.

figure.alt: Top row: two small green diamonds, then two big green diamonds with stripes. Bottom row: two small pink pentagons, then an empty box.

questions.explanation: Two things change across the top: the diamonds get bigger, and they get stripes. Two things stay the same: there are still two of them, and the colour does not change. Choice d added a third shape, but the number never changed.
questions.strategy: Write down what changes AND what stays the same. A wrong answer often changes something that should have stayed still.

questions.explanation: Two things change: the inside becomes dots, and the shape gets bigger. Choice b did not become dots. Choice c did not get bigger.
questions.strategy: Check what changed AND what stayed the same. Both are clues.

figure.alt: Top row: a small yellow ring, then a small pink ring, with stripes inside. Bottom row: a small yellow tall rectangle, then an empty box.

questions.explanation: Two things change: the color turns pink, and the inside becomes stripes. Choice b kept the old color. Choice c did not become stripes.
questions.strategy: Check what changed AND what stayed the same. Both are clues.

figure.alt: Top row: a small empty teal heart, then a big teal heart. Bottom row: a small empty teal cloud, then an empty box.

questions.explanation: Two things change: the shape fills in, and the shape gets bigger. Choice b never filled in. Choice c did not get bigger.
questions.strategy: Check what changed AND what stayed the same. Both are clues.

figure.alt: Top row: a green kite, then a smaller green kite turned a quarter turn. Bottom row: a green lightning bolt, then an empty box.

questions.explanation: Two rules apply at once: the figure shrinks, and it turns one quarter turn clockwise. Choice b shrank but did not turn. Choice c turned but did not shrink. Choice d turned the wrong way.
questions.strategy: Turning the wrong way is the most common slip. Decide clockwise or anticlockwise before you look at the choices.

figure.alt: Top row: four purple circles, then one purple circle. Bottom row: four orange squares, then an empty box.

questions.explanation: Four becomes one across the row. The column changes only the shape and the colour, never the count, so the answer keeps the bottom row's shape and colour and takes the top row's count of one.
questions.strategy: In a two-by-two, work across for one rule and down for the other. The answer obeys both.

figure.alt: Top row: an empty blue wide rectangle, then a big blue wide rectangle, with stripes inside. Bottom row: an empty blue trapezoid, then an empty box.

figure.alt: Top row: an empty green kite, then a big green kite, with dots inside. Bottom row: an empty green octagon, then an empty box.

questions.explanation: Two things change: the inside becomes dots, and the shape gets bigger. Choice b did not become dots. Choice c did not get bigger.

figure.alt: Top row: a red cross with dots, then a bigger red cross with stripes. Bottom row: a red plus sign with dots, then an empty box.

questions.explanation: Two rules run across the row: the figure grows, and the dots become flat sideways stripes. Choice d has stripes going the wrong way. Choice b kept the dots. Choice c stayed small.
questions.strategy: Stripes have a direction. Sideways stripes and up-and-down stripes are different answers.

figure.alt: Top row: an empty red bow tie, then a yellow bow tie, turned a quarter turn. Bottom row: an empty red heart, then an empty box.

questions.explanation: Three things change: the color turns yellow, the shape fills in, and the shape turns a quarter turn. Choice b kept the old color. Choice c never filled in.

figure.alt: Top row: a small green diamond, then a big red diamond, with a criss cross pattern inside. Bottom row: a small green arrow, then an empty box.

questions.explanation: Three things change: the shape gets bigger, the color turns red, and the inside becomes a criss cross pattern. Choice b did not get bigger. Choice c kept the old color.
questions.strategy: Each wrong answer follows all the rules but one. Find the one that breaks none.

figure.alt: Top row: two small teal semicircles, then three big teal semicircles turned upside down. Bottom row: two small pink flags, then an empty box.

questions.explanation: Three rules run across the row at once. The count goes from two to three. The shapes get bigger. And they flip upside down. Each wrong answer follows two rules and drops exactly one.
questions.strategy: When a question feels crowded, list the rules on your fingers. Then check the answer against every finger.

figure.alt: Top row: a small pink flag, then three big yellow flags. Bottom row: a small pink tall rectangle, then an empty box.

questions.explanation: Three things change: the color turns yellow, the shape gets bigger, and there are 3 of them instead. Choice b kept the old color. Choice c did not get bigger.

figure.alt: Top row: a blue crescent, then a blue crescent turned a quarter turn clockwise and shrunk. Bottom row: a blue leaf, then an empty box.

questions.explanation: Shrink, and turn one quarter turn clockwise. Choices b and c turn the right amount or more but the wrong way. Choice d turned correctly but stayed large.
questions.strategy: Three of the five choices here differ only in how far or which way the figure turned. Settle the turn first, then everything else.

figure.alt: Top row: a small empty purple heart, then three small green hearts, with flat stripes inside. Bottom row: a small empty purple half circle, then an empty box.

questions.explanation: Three things change: the inside becomes flat stripes, the color turns green, and there are 3 of them instead. Choice b did not become flat stripes. Choice c kept the old color.

figure.alt: Top row: an orange trapezoid, then a purple trapezoid, with stripes inside and turned three quarters of the way round. Bottom row: an orange upside-down triangle, then an empty box.

questions.explanation: Three things change: the shape turns three quarters of the way round, the inside becomes stripes, and the color turns purple. Choice b did not turn. Choice c did not become stripes.

figure.alt: Top row: five small green stars, then two big green stars. Bottom row: five small purple hexagons, then an empty box.

questions.explanation: Fewer shapes, and each one bigger. Five small becomes two large. The colour and the shape come from the bottom row and never change across.
questions.strategy: When shapes get fewer they often get bigger. Notice the trade: fewer means larger, more means smaller.

figure.alt: Top row: a yellow bowtie with stripes, then a red bowtie, solid and flipped a quarter turn. Bottom row: a yellow parallelogram with stripes, then an empty box.

questions.explanation: Three rules run at once: the colour turns red, the stripes fill in solid, and the figure turns a quarter turn. Choice b kept the stripes, c did not turn, d stayed yellow.
questions.strategy: With three rules, four of the five choices will each break exactly one. Find the one that breaks none.
